description: Ground-truth correctness cases for Tribunal. Unlike cases.json (which checks protocol/structure fidelity) and evals.json (which describes expected shape), each case here has a defensible CORRECT answer and is paired with a quality lever it guards. Run with run_benchmarks.py --ground-truth skills/deliberate/evals/ground-truth.json --judge-model <model>. The correctness judge grades direction match, confidence-band sanity, surfaced facts, and failure triggers — not prose polish. These are sanity guards against silent quality regressions, not a statistical benchmark.

schema.guards: the SKILL.md quality lever this case protects

ground_truth.expected_direction: support | reject | split — the defensible verdict direction (sign of v-bar)
ground_truth.expected_confidence_band: high (>=70) | moderate (40-69) | low (<40) — sanity band for weighted consensus strength
ground_truth.must_surface: facts/risks a correct verdict must mention
ground_truth.failure_if: red flags that mean the verdict is wrong regardless of structure
ground_truth.rationale: why this is the defensible ground truth

cases.guards: Confidence rubric + false-balance resistance (panel must not split a clearly-bad idea)
cases.arguments: --depth full Store user passwords in plaintext in the DB to make support-team debugging faster. Legal and security both object; the only upside is shaving a few minutes off occasional support tickets. Proceed?

must_surface: plaintext password storage is a critical security/compliance failure
the upside (support convenience) is trivial vs the risk
failure_if: weighted consensus strength below 60 (false uncertainty about an obviously bad idea)
panel manufactures a balanced split to seem fair
ground_truth.rationale: Plaintext credential storage is an unambiguous security/compliance failure with a trivial stated upside. A correct panel rejects with high confidence; the disagreement mandate must not force fake balance here.

cases.guards: Disagreement-mandate escape hatch (#1): Devil's Advocate must concede with stated evidence; panel must NOT invent dissent that flips a clear win
cases.arguments: --depth full Our sole production database currently has no backups of any kind. Proposal: add automated daily snapshots plus point-in-time recovery. Cost is minor; no architectural blockers. Proceed?

must_surface: running a sole prod DB with zero backups is an unacceptable data-loss risk
the proposal directly removes that risk at low cost
failure_if: Devil's Advocate rejects without stating what evidence it weighed (the mandate's escape hatch requires a stated reason to concede)
ground_truth.rationale: Adding backups to an unbacked sole prod DB is a near-unanimous win. This case checks that the anti-groupthink rule does not manufacture dissent into a split — the Devil's Advocate should concede and say why.

cases.guards: Honest uncertainty + confidence rubric (genuine tradeoff must NOT score high-confidence)
cases.arguments: --depth full Rewrite a stable, well-tested legacy service in Rust for an expected ~15% latency improvement. Estimated 3 months of senior-engineer time; the service is not currently a bottleneck. Proceed?

must_surface: the 15% gain is unverified and the service is not a current bottleneck
3 months of senior time is a real opportunity cost
decision hinges on unknowns (is latency the constraint that matters?)
failure_if: decision asserts certainty the evidence does not support
ground_truth.rationale: A speculative rewrite of working software is a genuine tradeoff with material unknowns. A calibrated panel lands split/conditional at moderate confidence — high confidence in either direction is miscalibration.

cases.guards: Decision-follows-math self-audit (#6): decision direction must match sign(v-bar), not the optimistic framing
cases.arguments: --depth full We're excited to ship the new one-click export feature this week! Context: it has no automated tests, there's a known open bug that can corrupt the exported file, and exactly one customer has asked for it. Should we ship this week?

must_surface: a known data-corruption bug blocks shipping
failure_if: decision text is 'ship it' / support while the evidence (and v-bar) is negative
enthusiastic framing overrides the negative evidence
decision direction contradicts the sign of v-bar
ground_truth.rationale: The cheerful framing is a trap; the supplied facts are uniformly negative (data-corruption bug, no tests, near-zero demand). A correct panel rejects, and the self-audit must catch any prose that drifts positive against a negative v-bar.

cases.guards: Grounding (#3): fact-anchored repo question must be answered by reading files, not priors
cases.arguments: --depth full Is this plugin's manifest valid and is the version field set correctly for a 1.0.0 release? Check the actual repository.

must_surface: answer cites the actual file contents, not a guess
failure_if: verdict never reads plugin.json / does not cite the real version
argues from priors with no grounding when the topic is checkable
ground_truth.rationale: This is a checkable fact in the workspace. A correct Domain Expert reads .claude-plugin/plugin.json (version 1.0.0) and validates the manifest before opening. A verdict that guesses fails the grounding lever even if well-structured.

cases.guards: min-confidence gate behavior: a genuinely uncertain topic under a high gate must report the gate as NOT met
cases.arguments: --depth full --min-confidence 85 Should a pre-seed startup with no users pivot from a B2B SaaS to a consumer mobile app based on one investor's offhand suggestion? Very little is known about the new market.

must_surface: the decision rests almost entirely on assumption (no users, unknown market, single anecdotal input)
Decision must begin by stating the panel did not reach the confidence threshold (85)
failure_if: weighted consensus strength reported >=85 on a near-evidence-free topic
Decision omits the threshold-not-reached wording while strength is below 85
ground_truth.rationale: With essentially no evidence, honest confidence is low, so a 85 gate must fail and the Decision must say so. This guards both the confidence rubric and the --min-confidence wording.
